stimuli.description: A virtual office environment (20 m²) with specific materials, lights, and cameras to achieve realism.

A binaural soundtrack composed of five disrupting sound sources (phone rings, machine noise from laptop/copier, mechanical systems, human-based sounds, acoustic effects from closing door/paper/pens) with an average LAeq = 55.6 dB.

tables.description: Acoustic and psychoacoustic mean values of the parameters calculated from the binaural recording in the office environment for Channel dx and sx.
Questions and ratings from the second section of the post-experimental survey, covering sound evaluation, thermal comfort, presence, immersivity, and cybersickness.
Mean (SD) and statistical analysis (t-value, p-value) of cognitive tasks (Magnitude-parity, Stroop, OSPAN) under quiet (Q) and noise (N) conditions.
Results of the Wilcoxon signed-rank test on thermal comfort (TSV, TCV, TPV).

limitations: The study was limited to the auditory senses; combined effects with other environmental drivers (e.g., visual, thermal) and different workplace layouts should be tested.
Future research should analyze the effect of different characteristics of the sound stimuli on dependent variables.
Further research should integrate physiological devices to measure objective harmful effects of noise on worker well-being and productivity.
